name: Transportation & Logistics
summary: Optimize logistics and supply chain operations.
description: Logistics UI UX design for fleet, dispatch and supply chain products: tracking, driver apps and operations dashboards that keep shipments moving on time.
image_alt: Truck on a highway at sunset, transportation and logistics industry
overview:
Logistics runs on timing. A late truck, a missed scan or an unclear delivery window costs money and customers, and the people dealing with it are often under pressure. Dispatchers watch many moving parts at once, while drivers and warehouse staff use apps one-handed, in poor light and with patchy signal.

I work with founders and product teams on web and mobile logistics products, from early prototypes to a design system engineers can build from directly. My experience designing monitoring dashboards, such as Nimbus, shapes how I surface exceptions, priorities and context, so teams can act before a delay becomes a problem.

challenges.title: Too many moving parts
challenges.text: Dispatchers track vehicles, orders and drivers at once, so the screen has to show what needs action first.

challenges.title: Field conditions
challenges.text: Drivers and warehouse staff use apps in vans, yards and loading bays, with gloves, glare and weak signal.

challenges.title: Exception handling
challenges.text: Delays, failed deliveries and damaged goods need clear flows, not workarounds by phone.

challenges.title: Many audiences
challenges.text: Shippers, carriers, drivers and end customers each need a different view of the same shipment.

faqs.question: Have you designed logistics products before?
faqs.answer: My closest published work is Nimbus, a monitoring dashboard that surfaces priority and context so teams know where to look. The same thinking applies to dispatch boards and tracking views, and I learn your operation in detail during discovery.

faqs.question: Can you design apps that work with weak or no signal?
faqs.answer: Yes. I design clear syncing, queued and offline states with your engineers, so drivers and warehouse staff always know whether their update has gone through.

faqs.question: Do you design for both web and mobile?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most logistics products need a web console for operations and mobile apps for drivers or customers, so I design them on one shared system.

faqs.question: Can you work with our existing design system?
faqs.answer: Yes. I can extend and clean up an existing system, or create one from scratch with tokens and components that match your codebase.

faqs.question: How do we start?
faqs.answer: Send me a short brief through the contact page. We will have a call about your product, users and timeline, and I will come back with a plan and quote.

approach.title: Discover
approach.text: Interviews with dispatchers, drivers and customers, and a look at how the work runs today, including the spreadsheets and phone calls.

approach.title: Map the flows

approach.title: Design and prototype

approach.title: Test in context

approach.title: Hand off
approach.text: A documented design system with tokens and components your engineers can build from.
